learningObjectives: Define what Templates are and why we use them.
Create a Template from an existing TestCase.

elements.text: Creating one individual TestCase per TestSheet row works, but it's repetitive and each TestCase needs individual maintenance — especially when a change falls in an area not suitable for a ReusableTestStepBlock. A Template solves this: it's a single TestCase that automatically generates a whole series of TestCases from the data in a TestSheet.

Designing cars: some are blue, some black, some silver; some manual, some automatic. It would be wasteful to design every variant from scratch. Instead, you design ONE base car (the blueprint) and spin off variations from it. A Template is exactly this blueprint — a base TestCase that spins off into a series of similar TestCases, each with a slightly different test focus.

elements.description: Designed to contain all possible paths of a linked TestSheet. When the Template is modified to reflect a SUT change, those modifications automatically feed through to every TestCase generated from it — centralizing maintenance and making full risk coverage far more time-efficient.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Converting a TestCase into a Template

elements.text: In our shirt-size example, the TestSheet covers 4 possible paths (S, M, L valid + XL invalid). We'll create a Template from an existing TestCase that already has References to ReusableTestStepBlocks in the Library, so it can generate all 4 TestCases.

elements.title: Prepare and convert
items: Right-click the folder → Resolve Reference, to remove/resolve References to the Library (as in AS1) — this lets you edit TestSteps freely without changing the shared Library.
Once ready, right-click the TestCase → Convert to Template.
A blue square with a "T" now appears in front of the TestCase icon — it is now a Template.
If needed, right-click again → Convert to TestCase to revert it.

elements.text: In the next lesson, this Template will be used to create the 4 TestCases defined in the linked TestSheet.

examPitfalls.title: Converting to a Template without resolving References first
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates convert a TestCase straight to a Template while it still has unresolved References to ReusableTestStepBlocks, then try to edit TestSteps — accidentally changing the shared Library.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Resolve References (right-click folder → Resolve Reference) before converting to a Template, so TestStep edits stay local to the Template.

examPitfalls.title: Not recognizing the Template icon
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Learners can't tell a Template apart from a regular TestCase in the Navigation pane.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A Template shows a blue square with a 'T' in front of the TestCase icon. No blue 'T' = still a plain TestCase.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Resolve Reference can always be undone
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates resolve a Reference, save the project, then try to undo it to restore the link to the Library.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Resolve Reference can only be undone via Tosca's Undo arrow BEFORE the project is saved. Once saved, the action is permanent.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why use a Template instead of creating 4 individual TestCases for the shirt-size scenario?

options.text: Tosca does not allow creating more than 1 TestCase manually.
A Template acts as a blueprint that automatically generates all 4 TestCases from the TestSheet, centralizing future maintenance.
Templates run faster than TestCases during execution.
Templates remove the need for a TestSheet entirely.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think of the car-design analogy — one blueprint, many variations.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Template is a blueprint TestCase. Linked to a TestSheet, it generates a full set of TestCases automatically, and future SUT changes only need to be applied once, in the Template.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before converting a TestCase to a Template, what should you check?

options.text: Nothing — Templates can always be converted directly with no preparation.
Whether it has References to ReusableTestStepBlocks that need to be resolved first.
Whether an ExecutionList already exists.
Whether the TestSheet already has 100 Instances.

practiceQuiz.hint: This step also appeared in AS1 when editing shared Library content.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Resolving References first (right-click → Resolve Reference) ensures that TestStep modifications made to the Template don't change the shared Library.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you convert a ready TestCase into a Template?

options.text: Right-click the TestSheet → Convert to Template.
Rename the TestCase to start with 'Template_'.
Right-click the TestCase → Convert to Template.
Drag the TestCase onto the TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a single right-click action on the TestCase itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Right-clicking the TestCase and selecting 'Convert to Template' converts it — shown by a blue square with a 'T' appearing in front of the icon.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can you visually confirm a TestCase has been successfully converted to a Template?

options.text: The icon disappears entirely.
The TestCase turns red.
A blue square containing a 'T' appears in front of the TestCase icon.
A green checkmark appears next to the TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a small blue marker with a letter on it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The blue square with a 'T' in front of the icon is Tosca's visual indicator that a TestCase is now a Template.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Log In Process exercise, how does a TestStep reference the project-wide Email Test Configuration Parameter?

options.text: {CP[Email]}
@Email@
$Email$
TestConfig.Email

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same syntax introduced back in AS1's Test Configuration Parameters lesson.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Test Configuration Parameters are referenced inside TestSteps using {CP[ParameterName]} — e.g. {CP[Email]} and {CP[Password]}, as recapped from AS1 Lesson 14.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You resolved a Reference on a Reusable TestStepBlock, then saved the Tosca project. You now want to undo the Resolve Reference action. What happens?

options.text: The project must be fully reinstalled to undo it.
Resolve Reference is always reversible via a dedicated 'Restore Reference' command.
Ctrl+Z always reverts it, saved or not.
It's too late — the Undo option to revert Resolve Reference is only available before the project is saved.

practiceQuiz.hint: Timing relative to saving is the key detail here.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Resolve Reference can only be undone via Tosca's Undo arrow, and only before the project has been saved. Once saved, the action is permanent.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the keyboard shortcut to quickly search for and add a TestStep or Reusable TestStepBlock to a TestCase?

options.text: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A
F9
Ctrl+J
Ctrl+T

practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+T opens the 'Add TestStep' search, letting you quickly find and insert TestSteps or Reusable TestStepBlocks into a TestCase.

quickRecap.value: A blueprint TestCase that generates a series of similar TestCases from a linked TestSheet.
Centralizes maintenance — one change in the Template feeds through to every generated TestCase.
Resolve any References to ReusableTestStepBlocks first.
Right-click TestCase → Convert to Template (shown by a blue 'T' icon).
Ctrl+T — search and insert a TestStep or Reusable TestStepBlock.
Reversible via Undo ONLY before the project is saved.
